deities: Lord Shiva as Ketaki Sangameshwara (Shiva Lingam)

history.dynasty: Modern structure (legendary origins in Krita Yuga)
history.period: Present structure about 200 years old per one source (verify); legend: Krita Yuga, Raja Kupendra of the Surya Vamsha; lingam said to have been established by Lord Brahma
history.summary: Sri Ketaki Sangameshwara Swamy Temple is the famous Shiva temple at Jharasangam, Sangareddy district (CSV town correct), in a densely forested area, drawing pilgrims from Telangana, Karnataka and Maharashtra. Legend: in the Krita Yuga, Surya Vamsha king Raja Kupendra suffered an incurable skin disease; while hunting he reached Ketaki Vanam, washed in a stream and was cured; Lord Shiva appeared in his dream and asked him to build a temple over the Shiva Lingam, which local legend says was established by Lord Brahma himself. The king converted the stream into a pushkarini called 'Astha Theertha Amrutha Gundam' (eight theerthas: Datha, Indira, Rudra, Soma, Varuna, Dharma, Rishi, Narayana), also known as 'Dakshina Kasi'. The temple's signature ritual: Ketaki flowers and leaves (normally never offered to Shiva) are used in worship here, with holy water from the pushkarini for yagnas and homas. Noted features: tall five-tier Rajagopuram with images of local gods in dancing forms, vast courtyard with herbal garden, medieval-style interior, and the continuously flowing water from the Shiva Lingam's panavattam. It is the most prominent of about 15 Shiva temples in the area and is considered a wish-fulfilling temple. CSV TOWN FLAG: the CSV district/state are correct (Sangareddy, Telangana); the older geocoder and some sources still list the old Medak district - this area was carved into Sangareddy in 2016.

name: Sri Ketaki Sangameshwara Swamy Temple, Jharasangam
town_description: Jharasangam is a village and mandal in the Zaheerabad area of Sangareddy district, Telangana (502246), set in a densely forested region; the temple lies a few kilometres from the mandal centre.

travel.airport: Rajiv Gandhi International Airport, Hyderabad - about 127 km (per xploreall; verify).
travel.railway: Zaheerabad railway station - about 5 km (per xploreall; verify).
travel.road: Jharasangam is connected by road to Zaheerabad and Sangareddy; MGBS Hyderabad to temple about 127 km by bus (per xploreall; verify).

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; Maha Shivaratri, Navaratri, Karthika Masam, Diwali and Ugadi are the festive peaks (per xploreall).
visitor_information.opening_hours: Sources conflict: 5:00 AM - 8:30 PM (xploreall); 5:30 AM - 9:00 PM (xploringdestinations); the temple's Facebook page lists 7:00 AM - 12:00 PM and 3:00 - 9:00 PM (verify before visiting).
